source_text: Quod autem dicunt reliqui eorum cultores etiam suorum quibusdam libris haec praecognita contineri, quamquam ex rebus inpletis conficta putanda sint, quae in eorum templis tam longo antea tempore populis eorum, si uera essent, innotescere debuerunt, sicut nostra non solum in ecclesiis nostris, uerum etiam — quod ad grauius testimonium contra omnes inimicos ualet — in iudaeorum synagogis antiquissima et notissima recitantur: tamen nec ipsa ista, quae ab eis uix raro et clanculo proferuntur, mouere nos debent, si cuiquam daemonum extortum est id prodere cultoribus suis, quod didicerat ex eloquiis prophetarum uel ex oraculis angelorum, quod cur non fieret, cum et ista non sit oppugnatio, sed adtestatio ueritatis? illud enim, quod solum ab eis flagitandum est, nec umquam antea protulerunt nec umquam postea nisi forte confictum proferre conabuntur, aliquid deos suos per uates suos contra deum Israhel ausos fuisse praedicere aut dicere. de quo deo doctissimi eorum auctores, qui omnia illa legere ac nosse potuerunt, magis quaesierunt, quis deus esset quam deum negare potuerunt. porro autem deus iste, quem nullus eorum negare ausus est uerum deum, qui et si negaret, non solum subiaceret debitis poenis, uerum etiam certis conuinceretur effectis: iste ergo deus, quem nemo, ut dixi, illorum negare ausus est uerum deum, illos falsos esse deos et omnino deserendos eorumque templa et simulacra euertenda per suos uates, hoc est prophetas, aperta denuntiatione praedixit, aperta potestate praecepit, aperta ueritate conpleuit. unde quis usque adeo desipiat, qui non eum potius colendum eligat, quem coli non prohibent, quos colebat? quem procul dubio cum colere coeperit, illos utique non est culturas, quos prohibet coli quem colit.
thought_title: The demons' late, coerced testimony only confirms the prophets
orientation: Augustine is answering the claim that pagan books also contained foreknowledge of the overthrow of the gods, and he is now arguing that even such rare, secret demonic predictions do not harm the Christian case.
pass_a_gloss: But what the remaining worshipers of them say, that these things foreknown are contained also in certain books of their own gods, although they should be thought invented from things fulfilled, which things, if they were true, ought to have become known to their peoples in their temples so long a time before, just as our things are recited not only in our churches but also — which avails for a weightier testimony against all enemies — in the synagogues of the Jews as most ancient and most known: nevertheless not even these very things, which are brought forward by them scarcely rarely and secretly, ought to move us, if from any demon it was extorted to reveal to his worshipers that which he had learned from the utterances of the prophets or from the oracles of angels, because why would this not happen, since this also is not an attack, but an attestation of the truth? For that thing, which alone is to be demanded from them, they neither brought forward ever before nor will they ever attempt to bring forward afterwards except perhaps invented, that their gods through their own prophets dared to predict or say anything against the God of Israel. About which God their most learned authors, who were able to read and know all those things, sought rather who God was than were able to deny God. Moreover this God, whom none of them dared to deny is the true God, who even if he were denied, would not only be subject to due punishments, but also would be convicted by certain effects: this God therefore, whom no one, as I said, of them dared to deny is the true God, predicted through his own prophets, that is, the prophets, with open denunciation that those are false gods and are to be utterly abandoned and their temples and idols are to be overthrown, commanded with open power, fulfilled with open truth. From which who would be so foolish, who would not choose rather to worship him, whom those whom he was worshiping do not forbid to be worshiped? Whom without doubt when he has begun to worship, he is certainly not going to worship those, whom he whom he worships forbids to be worshiped.

choices.why: Keeps the sense that these are the worshipers still left after the gods' overthrow, not just 'other' worshipers.

choices.english: should be thought invented from things fulfilled
choices.why: Preserves the passive periphrastic force and the idea that the books were fabricated after the events.
rejected: are to be regarded as made up

choices.why: Keeps the comparative force of grauius and the purpose sense of ad.
Renders the emphatic double adverb literally, showing how seldom and covertly these claims surface.
Keeps the violent, forced sense of extorqueo, implying the demon did not give this willingly.
Preserves the triple 'open' pattern (denuntiatione, potestate, ueritate) that Augustine builds rhetorically.

pass_b_english: But what the remaining worshipers of them say—that these things were foreknown and are contained in certain books of their own—although these must be thought fabricated from fulfilled events, even though, if they were true, they ought to have become known to their peoples in their temples so long before, just as our Scriptures are recited as most ancient and most widely known not only in our churches but also—which carries weightier testimony against all enemies—in the synagogues of the Jews. Nevertheless, even those things which are hardly ever and secretly brought forward by them ought not to move us, if it was extorted from some demon to reveal to his worshipers what he had learned from the utterances of the prophets or from the oracles of angels. Why should that not happen, since this is not an attack but an attestation of the truth? For the one thing that alone should be demanded from them—and they have never brought it forward before, nor will they ever attempt to bring it forward afterward except perhaps as something invented—is that their gods dared to predict or say anything through their own seers against the God of Israel. About this God, their most learned authors, who were able to read and know all those things, sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny God. Moreover, this God—whom none of them dared to deny is the true God, and even if anyone did deny it, he would not only be subject to due punishments but would also be convicted by certain effects—this God, then, whom no one of them, as I said, dared to deny is the true God, predicted through his own seers, that is, the prophets, with open denunciation that those gods are false and must be utterly abandoned and their temples and idols overthrown; he commanded it with open power; he fulfilled it with open truth. Who, then, would be so foolish as not to choose rather to worship him whom those he used to worship do not forbid him to worship? When he begins to worship him, he will certainly not worship those whom the one he worships forbids him to worship.

problems.quote: should be thought invented from things fulfilled
problems.source_quote: quamquam ex rebus inpletis conficta putanda sint
problems.why: Wrong modality: 'putanda sint' is passive 'should be thought,' but 'quamquam' makes this concessive ('although'), not the main claim. The main clause is missing.
problems.fix: although these must be thought fabricated from fulfilled events

problems.why: Double negative error: 'uix raro' means 'scarcely rarely' i.e. 'almost never' or 'hardly ever,' but 'scarcely rarely' in English is confusing/ambiguous.
problems.ruling: 'uix raro' means 'hardly ever'; 'scarcely rarely' is unidiomatic English, confusing readers.

problems.quote: sought rather who this God was than were able to deny that he was God
problems.source_quote: magis quaesierunt, quis deus esset quam deum negare potuerunt
problems.why: Wrong syntax: 'magis... quam' with indicative and infinitive means 'sought rather to find out who God was than [they were able] to deny God.' The English 'sought rather who this God was than were able to deny' is garbled.
problems.fix: sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny God
problems.ruling: 'magis quaesierunt...quam...potuerunt' means 'were more able to seek...than to deny'; English 'sought rather...than were able' is garbled.

edits.old: should be thought invented from things fulfilled
edits.new: although these must be thought fabricated from fulfilled events

edits.old: sought rather who this God was than were able to deny that he was God
edits.new: sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny God

fixed: Changed 'should be thought invented from things fulfilled' to 'although these must be thought fabricated from fulfilled events' to restore the concessive 'quamquam' clause.
Changed 'scarcely rarely and secretly' to 'hardly ever and secretly' to render 'uix raro' correctly.

Changed 'sought rather who this God was than were able to deny that he was God' to 'sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny God' to fix the garbled 'magis... quam' construction.

last_rejected.quote: if it was extorted from some demon to reveal to his worshipers
last_rejected.source_quote: si cuiquam daemonum extortum est id prodere cultoribus suis
last_rejected.why: Source has 'id' (it/this), referring to the prophetic content; English drops the object pronoun.
last_rejected.fix: if it was extorted from some demon to reveal this to his worshipers
last_rejected.ruling: 'id' is implicit in English 'to reveal'; object recoverable from context, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: Why should that not happen, since this is not an attack but an attestation of the truth?
last_rejected.source_quote: quod cur non fieret, cum et ista non sit oppugnatio, sed adtestatio ueritatis?
last_rejected.why: 'quod' refers to demons revealing prophetic content, not 'that not happen'; 'cur non fieret' = why it should not occur.
last_rejected.fix: And why should that not occur, since this is not an attack but an attestation of the truth?
last_rejected.ruling: English 'that' refers to same antecedent; 'why should that not happen' = 'cur non fieret,' same meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For the one thing that alone should be demanded from them
last_rejected.source_quote: illud enim, quod solum ab eis flagitandum est
last_rejected.why: 'flagitandum est' means 'must be demanded/required,' not 'should be'; the construction is impersonal necessity.
last_rejected.fix: For that which alone must be demanded from them
last_rejected.ruling: 'should be demanded' and 'must be demanded' both express necessity; within normal range, no mislead.

last_rejected.quote: sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny God
last_rejected.source_quote: magis quaesierunt, quis deus esset quam deum negare potuerunt
last_rejected.why: English adds extra 'God' at end, making it 'deny God' instead of 'deny [him/it]'; source means they sought who God was rather than were able to deny [the matter/God's existence].
last_rejected.fix: sought rather to learn who this God was than were able to deny it
last_rejected.ruling: 'deny God' correctly renders 'deum negare'; no meaning change, just pronoun choice within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: he would not only be subject to due punishments
last_rejected.why: English 'would be subject' misses the subjunctive contrary-to-fact; 'even if anyone did deny it, he would not only be subject' should be 'he would not only incur'.
last_rejected.fix: he would not only incur the due punishments
last_rejected.ruling: 'be subject to' is within normal range for 'subiaceret'; subjunctive contrary-to-fact already conveyed by 'even if anyone did deny'.
